Periodic cleanup runs (a) on every `derrick run` startup before doing anything else and (b) optionally as a launchd/systemd plist for long-lived setups. It walks worktree rows whose runs have crashed (no `finalize_worktree` event after a configurable TTL, default 24h), and either prunes them or marks them `Abandoned`. Same pattern for tickets stuck in `InReview` past a TTL: the foreman re-checks the PR and either transitions to `Done` (if observably merged), `Blocked` (if the PR was closed unmerged), or surfaces an escalation event. **There is no "trust eventually consistent state" path** — every long-lived state has an explicit reconciliation pass that can fail loud. | §8.2 / §9.C.5 / future T012 |
| D33 | **The foreman never has authoritative state independent of the substrate and git.** Where gastown's Mayor reads `gt convoy status` and trusts it, derrick's foreman treats its own poll as a hint and the substrate + git as the truth. Concretely: on every loop iteration the foreman (a) reads `bd ready`-equivalent tickets from the substrate, (b) for any in `InReview`, queries `git log` and `gh pr view` for the PR's actual state, (c) reconciles before dispatching new work. The dispatch is idempotent against state drift — if a ticket the substrate says is `Ready` is merged on main, the foreman corrects to `Done` and continues. | future T012 |
| D30 | **`derrick-tools` owns host CLI subprocess invocations; `derrick-models` owns the `Model` trait and providers.** Hosts (claude / codex / copilot) are invoked when a pipeline step sets `host:`. They receive an opaque prompt-as-argv (a slash command), they load their own context per the host rules, and derrick captures stdout. Providers are invoked when derrick needs a model completion via a structured `CompletionRequest` (assay reviewers, future direct-API calls). The same underlying binary (e.g. `codex`) may be reached via either path: as a host running a derrick-supplied prompt verbatim (`derrick-tools`), or as a backend for a model role that needs a structured completion (`derrick-models`'s `openai-cli` provider, etc.). The split is **invocation-shape-driven**, not binary-driven. | §3.1 / §6.5 / new T009 |
| D35 | **§8.6 alignment with D32: a closed-unmerged PR transitions its ticket to `Blocked`, not `Rejected`.** Earlier §8.6 prose used `Rejected` for both closed-unmerged and explicit user rejection. D32 distinguishes them: closed-unmerged is recoverable (a human may re-open with a new branch or explicitly reject), so the verifier moves to `Blocked` and waits for a human decision. `Rejected` is reserved for explicit user rejection via the §8.2 mutation API. The §8.6 diagram and verifier prose are updated to match; the T012 trait method `verify_ticket_unmerged` transitions to `Blocked`. | §8.6 / T012 |

T011 writes `.codex/instructions.md` (constitution + derrick.yaml reference) but does **not** install Codex tool-boundary hooks. When Codex grows a stable hook mechanism a follow-up ticket extends `derrick-adopt`. Claude Code hooks (D29 path b) remain mandatory; Copilot inline path (D29 path c) is unchanged. Users in `mode: copilot`/`crew` with codex hosts see a documented warning at init that Codex tool I/O is not scrubbed in v1. | §9.B.2 / §9.B.3 / T011 |
| D29 | **Scrub and caveman fire at every model boundary, not derrick's pipeline seams.** Three boundary classes: (a) derrick-internal — inline in `derrick-flow` and `derrick-substrate-native`; (b) host tool calls — `derrick init` writes `PreToolUse`+`PostToolUse` hooks in `.claude/settings.json` for Claude Code; Codex's equivalent is **deferred** (see D34); (c) Copilot dispatch — inline in `derrick-copilot` until Copilot's hook surface lands. Both directions matter: input (before embedding tool output into the next prompt) saves the most because of prompt caching; output (when an agent quotes tool output back) catches the second-order leakage. | §9.B.2 / §9.B.3 |
| D28 | **Supersedes D1 and D24 — GitHub-only distribution.** The `derrick.dev` domain was unavailable, so all derrick artefacts (install script, marketplace JSON, release binaries) live under `github.com/lgulliver/derrick`. The Claude Code marketplace JSON is fetched from `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lgulliver/derrick/main/marketplace.json`. There is no longer a separate marketplace host to health-check, so D24's fallback logic collapses to a single GitHub-releases path; transient GitHub unavailability surfaces as a normal network error to the user with the documented recovery (`gh release download` or manual binary install). | §11 |
| D36 | **Headless subprocess Write permissions: pre-create feature dirs.** `claude --print` prompts for Write tool permission when creating files in directories that don't yet exist, even with a `permissions.allow` block in `.claude/settings.json` (the block format did not suppress the prompt in practice). Resolved: `derrick init` and the pipeline runner pre-create `.specify/features/` before invoking any host step, so the directory exists and the Write prompt is not triggered. Long-term: `derrick-flow` creates the feature dir as the first act of the `specify` step, before the host invocation. | §5.3 / T013 |
| D37 | **Codex requires an interactive TTY; assay skips in headless mode.** `codex` exits immediately with "stdin is not a terminal" when invoked from a background subprocess, making the assay step unusable in unattended `derrick run` invocations. Resolution: `derrick-flow` detects `!isatty(stdin)` and, when the assay step's reviewer is a codex-family host, falls back to `claude` as the reviewer (with the assay role model). The fallback is logged as an `EscalationNote` event so the audit trail records that the interactive reviewer was substituted. Until this is implemented, `--skip assay` is the documented workaround. | §7 / D5 |
| D38 | **Each pipeline run gets an isolated git worktree (§9.C.5).** `run_pipeline_from` calls `git worktree add -b derrick/<run-id> .derrick/worktrees/<run-id> HEAD` before the first step and `git worktree remove --force` on completion. The substrate's `reserve_worktree` / `close_worktree` methods are added to the `Substrate` trait so the `Runner` can track the lifecycle via `Arc<dyn Substrate>`. All host-request CWDs and bash `current_dir` use the worktree path; `relative_to_root` and manifest paths continue to use `repo_root`. Degradation: if `git worktree add` fails (no binary, dirty index), setup logs a warning and the run continues in `repo_root` — no crash. | §9.C.5 |
| D40 | **Token counts and cost estimates are tracked per pipeline step and per run.** `CompletionResponse.tokens_in/out` are threaded through `StepExecution` → `StepRecord` → `ManifestStep` and accumulated into `RunManifest.tokens_in/out`. `RunOutcome.cost_estimate_usd(model_name)` uses a built-in pricing table (`builtin_cost_hint`) seeded with current list prices for Claude Opus/Sonnet/Haiku, GPT-4o/mini, and Gemini 2.5. Host-subprocess steps (claude CLI, copilot CLI) report zero at this layer; their token counts appear separately in `derrick gain` via Claude Code JSONL. `derrick gain --run <id>` shows a per-step breakdown from the manifest; session-level `gain` shows estimated dollar cost alongside token totals. | §9.B / `derrick-models` |
| D39 | **Adversarial code review fires before every PR, not after.** `derrick ticket code-review <id> --branch <branch> --round N` diffs `origin/<base>...<branch>` (three-dot), passes the diff + ticket requirements to a configured reviewer role, and exits 0 (pass) or 3 (issues found). Hands must call this and get a pass before calling `derrick ticket review`. Auto-remediation is hand-driven: the hand reads `.derrick/reviews/<id>/round-N.md`, fixes, and retries up to `tools.code_review.rounds` times. Beyond that, the hand surfaces the report to the human. Exit code 3 (not 1) lets hands distinguish "fix needed" from infrastructure errors. Disabled by default (`tools.code_review.enabled: false`). | §8.6 / AGENTS.md hand protocol |
| D41 | **OpenCode is a first-class host.** `derrick-tools` gains an `OpencodeHost` adapter that invokes `opencode run "<prompt>" --dir <cwd> [--dangerously-skip-permissions]`. `derrick-scrub` gains an `opencode` rule set that strips the startup banner, tool-use progress lines, spinner frames, thinking markers, and cost footers. Specialist sub-agents are published under `.opencode/agents/` with opencode frontmatter (`mode: agent`). The `HostRegistry` default set now includes `opencode` alongside `claude`, `codex`, and `copilot`. | §6.5 / `derrick-tools` / `derrick-scrub` |
| D42 | **Full courtroom pattern: adversarial cross-model deliberation with auto-revise loop.** Assay implements the structured Claude-prosecutes / Codex-cross-examines / Claude-rebuts / Codex-deliberates cycle from the courtroom pattern. Default rounds: 10. Constitution violations are parsed and enforced as non-negotiable gates (override requires human approval). When the revise loop exhausts configured rounds, derrick prompts the user to continue or halt. Progress is streamed in real-time (round N/M, verdict, phase name) instead of a spinner. The loop switches from a `for` to a `while` to allow dynamic round extension at user request. | §7 / `derrick-flow/src/assay.rs` |
| D43 | **Roughneck: LLM output compression via prompt injection.** A new crate `derrick-roughneck` appends a compression instruction to every model request, asking the model to emit a compressed form of its output before handoff. Three levels: `lite` (~30%), `full` (~65%, default), `ultra` (~75%). Config: `tools.roughneck.{enabled,level,compress_memory}`. Per-step manifest field `roughneck_tokens_saved` records estimated savings. TUI Tokens tab surfaces roughneck savings alongside scrub. | §3.1 / §9.B.2a / §10.1 |
| D44 | **`derrick-scrub` records bytes_raw and bytes_saved per step in the manifest.** The scrub crate already existed; this decision adds structured telemetry so `derrick gain` and the TUI can show per-step context reduction, not a binary "scrub on/off". Config: `tools.output_compression.enabled`. | §9.B.2 / §10.1 |
| D45 | **`tokens_in` correction: `max(cli_reported, prompt_len/4)`.** `claude --output-format json` under-reports input tokens (direct message only, not full session context). Fix: derrick records the CLI value and a character-count estimate and stores the larger. Conservative but prevents systematic under-counting on cached-prefix sessions. | §9.B.7 / §10.1 |
| D46 | **Run resume via `prompt_key`: idempotent retry for incomplete runs.** Each run computes a 12-hex SHA-256 prefix of the normalised prompt (`prompt_key`). `derrick add` auto-resumes the most recent incomplete run with the same key instead of starting fresh. `--force` overrides. `resume_of` in the manifest tracks lineage. Completed runs are never auto-resumed. | §10.2 |
| D47 | **Bridge auto-remediation: terminal ticket delete+recreate; active ticket skip.** When creating tickets, bridge checks for existing tickets with the same feature identity. Terminal-state tickets (Done/Cancelled) are deleted and recreated. Non-terminal tickets are reused (skipped). Both rules fire per-ticket so partial batches are handled correctly. | §8.2.1 |
| D48 | **Assay headless mode: only `reject` blocks the pipeline.** When `!isatty(stdin)`, assay runs without interactive prompts. `revise` and `accept` are both treated as pass; round exhaustion without `reject` logs a warning and continues. The hard rounds limit applies. Enables fully unattended CI runs. | §7 headless / §4 assay step |
| D49 | **Constitution seeding in `derrick init` wizard.** When no existing constitution is found and speckit is unavailable for interactive authoring, the wizard prompts the user to enter constitution content directly. The text is written to `.specify/constitution.md` as real content (no banner stub). `--constitution-stub` still writes the banner for users who prefer to author separately. | §5.2 Step 5 |
| D50 | **`derrick init` creates an initial commit when the repo has no HEAD.** After writing all init files, if the repo has no commits yet, the wizard runs `git add -A && git commit -m "chore: derrick init"`. Required because `derrick add` creates git worktrees, which require at least one commit. | §5.2 Step 7 |
| D51 | **Pipeline step order fix: `tasks` runs before `analyze`.** Task generation depends on the accepted plan but not on codebase analysis. `analyze` then has the full task list available as context. Canonical order: `specify → clarify → plan → tasks → analyze → assay → bridge → foreman`. All pipeline config, step descriptions, and the §9.B.1 table updated to match. | §4 pipeline yaml / §9.B.1 / §9.C |
| D52 | **`derrick switch`: solo → crew upgrade command.** New subcommand upgrades a repo from `mode: solo` to `mode: crew` (or `copilot` via `--mode`). Patches `tools.substrate.mode`, adds `peers:` stanza, writes foreman defaults. Idempotent. `--dry-run` previews the yaml diff. | §5.2.2 / §11 |
| D53 | **`derrick upgrade` name reserved for binary self-update.** The subcommand is registered in the CLI but not yet implemented. It prints a clear "not yet available" message rather than a "command not found" error, preserving the name for the future self-update feature (check GitHub releases, download, replace running binary). | §11 |

### Remaining open questions

None blocking. All v1 design questions resolved (D1–D53).

New questions raised during implementation will be tracked as
GitHub issues with the `design-question` label, and locked-in
answers folded back into this file as further `D` entries with
a section back-reference.

## 13. Naming

We're calling it **derrick**. Reasons:

- The load-bearing structure over an oil well — fits the gastown /
 petroleum metaphor lineage.
- Single point that lifts every length of pipe in and out — matches the
 "single point of entry" framing.
- Short, lowercase, doesn't collide with an existing common CLI on PATH
 (verified locally — there's no `derrick` in homebrew core formulas at
 the time of writing; will re-check before publishing).

Binary: `derrick`. Repo: `derrick`. Plugin: `derrick`.

### 3.1 Components

Rust workspace. One binary (`derrick`), many crates so individual
modules can be tested, profiled, and (later) ported in isolation.

| Component | Crate | Purpose |
|---|---|---|

| Orchestrator | `crates/derrick-flow` | Pipeline state machine, step runner, structured logging (`tracing`) |
| Tool adapters | `crates/derrick-tools` | Thin wrappers around `claude`, `codex`, `copilot`, `specify` (tokio::process) |
| Assay | `crates/derrick-assay` | Adversarial plan review; calls the reviewer role(s) directly (see §7) |
| Memory | `crates/derrick-memory` | Seeds host memory files on init + per-step context budgets |
| Scrubber | `crates/derrick-scrub` | Subprocess output filter; rules-based sanitizer for cargo/git/gh/claude/opencode output before writing to step logs. Reduces context bytes fed to the LLM in subsequent steps. Per-tool rule sets in `src/rules/<tool>.rs`. Pure functions, zero-copy where possible. |
| Roughneck | `crates/derrick-roughneck` | LLM output compression via prompt injection. Three levels: `lite` (~30% savings), `full` (~65%, default), `ultra` (~75%). Fires after every model boundary to compress the response before it enters the next step's context. |
| Caveman | `crates/derrick-caveman` | Text compressor for inter-step handoff, pure functions |
| Copilot | `crates/derrick-copilot` | Dispatches steps or tickets to Copilot agents (CLI + Workspace API) |
| Models | `crates/derrick-models` | Provider trait; adapters for API providers, local runtimes, CLI shells (see §6.5) |

Codex hook installation deferred (D34); T011 writes `.codex/instructions.md` only. |

- **Lightweight at runtime.** `derrick scrub` wraps every subprocess; cold-start
 cost matters. Rust gives us near-zero overhead.

- **Async fan-out.** Multi-reviewer assay, parallel observability reads, and

- **Single static binary.** `cargo build --release` → one file, easy to ship

- **SQLite via `rusqlite`** (bundled) or `sqlx` — both first-class.

(if we ever add one) means shelling to a Go CLI, not vendoring its types.

# Token Economist

You own `derrick-scrub` (subprocess filter), `derrick-caveman`
(text compressor), `derrick-memory` (memory seeding), and the
telemetry path that powers `derrick gain`. The three pillars are
your job to keep honest.

## In scope

- Scrubber rules per tool in `crates/derrick-scrub/src/rules/<tool>.rs`.
  Each rule is a pure function over a byte slice.
- Caveman shaping in `crates/derrick-caveman/`. Three intensity
  levels (`lite | full | ultra`). **Byte-identical to the caveman
  skill at matched intensities** (D7). Identifiers, paths, error
  messages preserved verbatim.
- Both scrub and caveman fire at **every** model boundary (D29),
  not just derrick's pipeline seams: derrick-internal handoffs,
  host tool calls (via hooks `flow-engineer`/`adopt` writes),
  and Copilot dispatch in both directions (input + output). The
  hot path is *input* — the bytes about to be embedded in the
  next prompt — because prompt caching compounds the saving.
- Memory seeding on `derrick init`: project / reference /
  feedback / lessons entries, namespaced `derrick/<site>/...`.
- Cross-feature lessons extraction with the quality gate from D9
  (reference a ticket id or constitution section anchor, else
  discard).
- Prompt caching strategy (DESIGN.md §9.B.4): constitution +
  derrick.yaml + memory seeds in the cached prefix of every call.
- Lazy artifact loading (§9.B.5): a step only loads declared
  `inputs:`.
- Telemetry (§9.B.7): per-step token estimates, transcript parsing
  for Claude Code sessions, `derrick gain` / `derrick gain
  --pillars` output.

## Out of scope

- Pipeline orchestration (`flow-engineer`).
- Provider call mechanics (`integrations-engineer`).
- Substrate writes (`substrate-engineer`).

## Working agreement

- Pure functions wherever possible. Scrubber and caveman are
  testable as `(input, intensity) -> output`. No I/O inside them.
- Caveman drift from the skill is a bug. Maintain a corpus of
  paired inputs in `crates/derrick-caveman/tests/corpus/` that
  asserts byte-identity at each intensity.
- Scrubber rules ship with a regression test per rule. Adding a
  rule without a test is a review-blocking issue.
- Memory writes are *additive* and *namespaced*. `derrick init
  --unmemoize` removes only entries under `derrick/<site>/`.
- `derrick gain` numbers must reconcile. If reported savings don't
  add up to (raw − actual), the report is wrong.

## Stop conditions (escalate)

- A request to call the caveman skill recursively via claude on
  the hot path (D8 explicitly forbids this for the default path —
  fallback to skill is for unknown artifact types only).
- A request to log a key, token, or other secret at any verbosity.

## Key references

- DESIGN.md §9 — the three pillars.
- DESIGN.md §9.A — memory layers.
- DESIGN.md §9.B — token knobs.
- DESIGN.md §9.B.7 — transcript-parsed telemetry (D14).
- D7, D8, D9, D14 — your decisions.

No code-graph or indexing layer exists today; derrick is a mature 18-crate native Rust workspace built around three pillars (memory, tokens, parallelism), ships as a single static binary, configures hosts via `derrick-adopt` (`.claude/settings.json` hooks, `.codex/instructions.md`), and explicitly avoids external SaaS / runtimes.

Three genuine forks materially change the design, so let me confirm them before writing the plan.

input.content:
# Plan: native code-graph index for derrick (`derrick-index`)

## Context

CodeGraph (https://github.com/colbymchenry/codegraph) is a Node/TypeScript
tool that pre-indexes a repo into a SQLite + FTS5 knowledge graph (symbols,
references, call relationships) and exposes it to coding agents over **MCP**.
Its benchmark across 7 repos shows ~35% cheaper, ~57% fewer tokens, ~71%
fewer tool calls — the win comes from agents *querying the graph directly*
instead of fanning out across grep/glob/Read (and the Explore sub-agents
they spawn).

derrick is built around three pillars — **memory, tokens, parallelism** —
and a hard rule that nothing ships unless it's memory-aware, token-efficient,
and parallel-safe (DESIGN §9). A code-graph index is squarely a **Tokens
pillar** feature: it replaces expensive file-reads with cheap structured
queries, which then feed through the existing scrub/caveman/`derrick gain`
machinery.

Today derrick has **no indexing, search, or RAG layer** (verified — no
tree-sitter/ctags/tantivy/FTS anywhere in the workspace). Repo context
reaches agents only via host-loaded file reads (D30) filtered by scrub/caveman
at model boundaries (D29). This feature adds the missing layer.

**Decisions taken (this planning session):**
- **Native Rust**, not a Node wrapper — preserves the single-static-binary,
  no-external-runtime, batteries-included ethos and the D11 substrate/scope
  discipline. We adopt CodeGraph's proven *data model* (symbols + `references`
  edges + FTS5) as the reference design without its runtime.
- **MCP server** as the agent-facing surface — the benchmark win requires
  agents to query directly; CLI-via-Bash doesn't steer them reliably. This
  introduces MCP into derrick for the first time (today it uses host CLI
  subprocess + hooks), so it's a genuine new seam.
- **Focused v1 scope**: symbol index + full-text search + caller/callee/impact,
  for the languages derrick users work in (**Rust, TS/JS, Python, Go**). Defer
  the long tail (20+ langs, framework-aware routes, iOS/RN cross-language
  bridging) — most of it won't move derrick's own token numbers.

## Process gates (do these first)

This is a net-new crate, net-new vocabulary, and a net-new architectural seam
(MCP). Per CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md house rules it cannot just be coded:

1. **`design-keeper`** — record a new decision **D54** ("native code-graph
   index, MCP-exposed, own SQLite DB, focused language set") and lock the
   vocabulary (see naming note below). Add a DESIGN.md §9.B knob entry and a
   short §3.1 component row.
2. **`rust-architect`** — sign off the crate seam: the public query trait, the
   MCP transport choice (`rmcp` vs. a minimal stdio JSON-RPC server), and the
   decision to use a **separate** SQLite DB rather than the substrate DB.
3. Implementation then dispatches to **Copilot/Codex** per the orchestration
   model (Claude orchestrates; production code goes through review/impl hosts).
   Specialist owners: **token-economist** (gain telemetry), **integrations-
   engineer** (host/MCP config in `derrick-adopt`), **flow-engineer** (optional
   pipeline auto-query later).

**Naming** (for design-keeper to lock): the petroleum metaphor suggests
`survey` (a seismic survey maps subsurface structure before drilling) or
`core` (a core sample). Working name in this plan is `derrick-index` /
`derrick index …`; final name is design-keeper's call.

## Architecture

### New crate: `crates/derrick-index`

Pure-Rust, leaning on crates already in (or compatible with) the workspace:

| Concern | Choice | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Parsing | `tree-sitter` + `tree-sitter-{rust,typescript,javascript,python,go}` | Per-language symbol + reference extraction. Static-linked grammars — no runtime dep. |
| Storage | `rusqlite` (already a workspace dep, `bundled`) + **FTS5** | Verify `bundled` enables `SQLITE_ENABLE_FTS5`; add `bundled-full` or the `fts5` feature if not. |
| Watch | `notify` (already a workspace dep) | Debounced re-index, mirrors CodeGraph's watcher. |
| Parallel build | `tokio` fan-out (or `rayon`) over files | Parsing is embarrassingly parallel (Parallelism pillar). |
| MCP | `rmcp` (official Rust MCP SDK) — rust-architect to confirm | Fallback: hand-rolled stdio JSON-RPC, since the tool surface is tiny. |

### Storage — its own DB, not the substrate

Index lives at **`.derrick/index.db`**, owned solely by `derrick-index`.
Rationale: AGENTS.md house rule forbids touching SQLite from outside
`derrick-substrate-native`; the index has a totally different schema, lifecycle
(rebuildable cache, gitignored), and concurrency profile. Keep it separate.
Add `.derrick/index.db*` to the init `.gitignore` block.

Reference schema (CodeGraph-shaped, minimal):
- `files(id, path, lang, size, mtime, content_hash)`
- `symbols(id, file_id, name, kind, start_line, end_line, signature)`
- `refs(src_symbol_id, dst_symbol_id, kind)`  — kind ∈ {call, reference}
- `symbols_fts` — FTS5 virtual table over `name`/`signature` for instant search
- Concurrency: single-writer + small reader pool, same pattern as
  `derrick-substrate-native` (`READER_POOL_SIZE`).

### MCP tool surface (focused)

Launched via `derrick index serve --mcp` (stdio). Four tools, names mirroring
CodeGraph's proven set:
- `derrick_index_search(query)` → FTS symbol hits with file:line.
- `derrick_index_context(query)` → entry points + related symbols + snippets
  (the "one call answers the architecture question" tool that drives the win).
- `derrick_index_impact(symbol)` → callers / callees / impact radius.
- `derrick_index_status()` → freshness; lists pending files.

**Freshness** (mirror CodeGraph's three layers so agents never get a silent
stale answer): (1) `notify` watcher + debounce re-index; (2) per-file staleness
banner in tool responses telling the agent to `Read` a pending file directly;
(3) connect-time `(size,mtime)`+hash reconciliation before the first query.

### CLI surface

New nested subcommand group, following the existing `Ticket`/`Foreman`/`Stack`
pattern in `crates/derrick-cli/src/commands/mod.rs` + a handler module
`crates/derrick-cli/src/commands/index.rs` dispatched from
`crates/derrick-cli/src/lib.rs`:
- `derrick index build` — full (re)index.
- `derrick index serve --mcp` — run the MCP server (what hosts launch).
- `derrick index search|context|impact <args>` — ad-hoc CLI parity with the
  MCP tools (also lets agents use it via Bash where MCP isn't wired).
- `derrick index status` — freshness report.

### Host wiring (`derrick-adopt`)

`derrick-adopt` already writes host config (`.claude/settings.json` hooks,
`.codex/instructions.md`, opencode agents — D29/D34/D41). Extend it to register
the MCP server for each detected host that supports MCP:
- Claude Code: add `mcpServers.derrick-index` stanza (`command: derrick`,
  `args: ["index","serve","--mcp"]`).
- opencode / codex / copilot: equivalent MCP stanzas where the host supports
  them; document the gap where it doesn't (same posture as D34's Codex-hooks
  deferral).
- Auto-allow permissions for the index tools, as CodeGraph does for Claude.
- `derrick uninstall` must strip these stanzas (reverse cleanly, per D16).

### Pillar integration

- **Tokens**: add an `index` line to `derrick gain` / `gain --pillars`
  (file-reads avoided, est. tokens saved). token-economist owns this telemetry
  so the numbers reconcile.
- **Memory**: seed the index DB location as *reference memory* on `derrick init`
  (where the graph lives), namespaced `derrick/<site>/`.
- **Parallelism**: build fans out per-file; the index DB is shared **read-only**
  across worktree runs (D38) — every concurrent run queries one index. Reader
  pool keeps that safe.

## Phased delivery

1. **Gates**: D54 + naming (design-keeper); seam sign-off (rust-architect).
2. **Core crate**: `derrick-index` — schema, tree-sitter extraction for the 4
   languages, `build`, FTS search. Unit tests on a fixture repo per language.
3. **CLI**: `index build|search|context|impact|status` subcommands.
4. **MCP server**: `index serve --mcp` exposing the 4 tools + freshness layers.
5. **Host wiring**: `derrick-adopt` MCP stanzas + permissions + uninstall
   reversal.
6. **Telemetry**: `derrick gain` index line; reference-memory seed.
7. **Watcher**: `notify`-based debounced auto-sync + staleness banners.

## Files to create / modify

- **New**: `crates/derrick-index/` (Cargo.toml, src/lib.rs, src/schema.rs,
  src/parse/{rust,ts,python,go}.rs, src/db.rs, src/mcp.rs, src/watch.rs,
  tests/corpus/).
- **New**: `crates/derrick-cli/src/commands/index.rs`.
- **Modify**: root `Cargo.toml` (workspace member + tree-sitter/rmcp deps);
  `crates/derrick-cli/src/commands/mod.rs` (add `Index` command + nested enum);
  `crates/derrick-cli/src/lib.rs` (dispatch arm);
  `crates/derrick-adopt/src/lib.rs` (MCP stanza writer + uninstall reversal);
  `crates/derrick-observe`/`derrick gain` path (telemetry line);
  `DESIGN.md` (§3.1 row, §9.B knob, §12 D54);
  `.claude/agents/` (consider an `index-engineer` scope, or fold into
  token-economist — design-keeper's call).
- **Init template**: add `.derrick/index.db*` to the gitignore block.

## Verification

- **Per-language extraction**: fixture repo per language under

Pure-Rust, leaning on crates already in (or compatible with) the workspace:

| Concern | Choice | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Parsing | `tree-sitter` + `tree-sitter-{rust,typescript,javascript,python,go}` | Per-language symbol + reference extraction. Static-linked grammars — no runtime dep. |
| Storage | `rusqlite` (already a workspace dep, `bundled`) + **FTS5** | Verify `bundled` enables `SQLITE_ENABLE_FTS5`; add `bundled-full` or the `fts5` feature if not. |
| Watch | `notify` (already a workspace dep) | Debounced re-index, mirrors CodeGraph's watcher. |
| Parallel build | `tokio` fan-out (or `rayon`) over files | Parsing is embarrassingly parallel (Parallelism pillar). |
| MCP | `rmcp` (official Rust MCP SDK) — rust-architect to confirm | Fallback: hand-rolled stdio JSON-RPC, since the tool surface is tiny. |

### Storage — its own DB, not the substrate

Index lives at **`.derrick/index.db`**, owned solely by `derrick-index`.
Rationale: AGENTS.md house rule forbids touching SQLite from outside
`derrick-substrate-native`; the index has a totally different schema, lifecycle
(rebuildable cache, gitignored), and concurrency profile. Keep it separate.
Add `.derrick/index.db*` to the init `.gitignore` block.

Reference schema (CodeGraph-shaped, minimal):
- `files(id, path, lang, size, mtime, content_hash)`
- `symbols(id, file_id, name, kind, start_line, end_line, signature)`
- `refs(src_symbol_id, dst_symbol_id, kind)`  — kind ∈ {call, reference}
- `symbols_fts` — FTS5 virtual table over `name`/`signature` for instant search
- Concurrency: single-writer + small reader pool, same pattern as
  `derrick-substrate-native` (`READER_POOL_SIZE`).

### MCP tool surface (focused)

Launched via `derrick index serve --mcp` (stdio). Four tools, names mirroring
CodeGraph's proven set:
- `derrick_index_search(query)` → FTS symbol hits with file:line.
- `derrick_index_context(query)` → entry points + related symbols + snippets
  (the "one call answers the architecture question" tool that drives the win).
- `derrick_index_impact(symbol)` → callers / callees / impact radius.
- `derrick_index_status()` → freshness; lists pending files.

**Freshness** (mirror CodeGraph's three layers so agents never get a silent
stale answer): (1) `notify` watcher + debounce re-index; (2) per-file staleness
banner in tool responses telling the agent to `Read` a pending file directly;
(3) connect-time `(size,mtime)`+hash reconciliation before the first query.

### CLI surface

New nested subcommand group, following the existing `Ticket`/`Foreman`/`Stack`
pattern in `crates/derrick-cli/src/commands/mod.rs` + a handler module
`crates/derrick-cli/src/commands/index.rs` dispatched from
`crates/derrick-cli/src/lib.rs`:
- `derrick index build` — full (re)index.
- `derrick index serve --mcp` — run the MCP server (what hosts launch).
- `derrick index search|context|impact <args>` — ad-hoc CLI parity with the
  MCP tools (also lets agents use it via Bash where MCP isn't wired).
- `derrick index status` — freshness report.

### Host wiring (`derrick-adopt`)

`derrick-adopt` already writes host config (`.claude/settings.json` hooks,
`.codex/instructions.md`, opencode agents — D29/D34/D41). Extend it to register
the MCP server for each detected host that supports MCP:
- Claude Code: add `mcpServers.derrick-index` stanza (`command: derrick`,
  `args: ["index","serve","--mcp"]`).
- opencode / codex / copilot: equivalent MCP stanzas where the host supports
  them; document the gap where it doesn't (same posture as D34's Codex-hooks
  deferral).
- Auto-allow permissions for the index tools, as CodeGraph does for Claude.
- `derrick uninstall` must strip these stanzas (reverse cleanly, per D16).

### Pillar integration

- **Tokens**: add an `index` line to `derrick gain` / `gain --pillars`
  (file-reads avoided, est. tokens saved). token-economist owns this telemetry
  so the numbers reconcile.
- **Memory**: seed the index DB location as *reference memory* on `derrick init`
  (where the graph lives), namespaced `derrick/<site>/`.
- **Parallelism**: build fans out per-file; the index DB is shared **read-only**
  across worktree runs (D38) — every concurrent run queries one index. Reader
  pool keeps that safe.

## Phased delivery

1. **Gates**: D54 + naming (design-keeper); seam sign-off (rust-architect).
2. **Core crate**: `derrick-index` — schema, tree-sitter extraction for the 4
   languages, `build`, FTS search. Unit tests on a fixture repo per language.
3. **CLI**: `index build|search|context|impact|status` subcommands.
4. **MCP server**: `index serve --mcp` exposing the 4 tools + freshness layers.
5. **Host wiring**: `derrick-adopt` MCP stanzas + permissions + uninstall
   reversal.
6. **Telemetry**: `derrick gain` index line; reference-memory seed.
7. **Watcher**: `notify`-based debounced auto-sync + staleness banners.

## Files to create / modify

- **New**: `crates/derrick-index/` (Cargo.toml, src/lib.rs, src/schema.rs,
  src/parse/{rust,ts,python,go}.rs, src/db.rs, src/mcp.rs, src/watch.rs,
  tests/corpus/).
- **New**: `crates/derrick-cli/src/commands/index.rs`.
- **Modify**: root `Cargo.toml` (workspace member + tree-sitter/rmcp deps);
  `crates/derrick-cli/src/commands/mod.rs` (add `Index` command + nested enum);
  `crates/derrick-cli/src/lib.rs` (dispatch arm);
  `crates/derrick-adopt/src/lib.rs` (MCP stanza writer + uninstall reversal);
  `crates/derrick-observe`/`derrick gain` path (telemetry line);
  `DESIGN.md` (§3.1 row, §9.B knob, §12 D54);
  `.claude/agents/` (consider an `index-engineer` scope, or fold into
  token-economist — design-keeper's call).
- **Init template**: add `.derrick/index.db*` to the gitignore block.

## Verification

- **Per-language extraction**: fixture repo per language under
  `crates/derrick-index/tests/`; assert symbols/refs counts and FTS hits.
- **End-to-end build**: `derrick index build` on derrick's own repo; spot-check
  `derrick index impact <a known symbol>` returns real callers/callees.
- **MCP smoke**: launch `derrick index serve --mcp`, drive the four tools over
  stdio JSON-RPC, confirm well-formed responses + staleness banner when a file
  is edited mid-session.
- **Host integration**: run `derrick init`/adopt in a scratch repo, confirm the
  `mcpServers.derrick-index` stanza lands in `.claude/settings.json` and that
  `derrick uninstall` removes it.
- **Pillar proof (the actual goal)**: replicate CodeGraph's benchmark shape —
  run a headless `claude -p` architecture question on a sample repo **with** and
  **without** the index MCP server enabled; compare tokens / tool calls / cost.
  Wire the delta into `derrick gain` and confirm the numbers reconcile.
- **Workspace**: `cargo build --release` still produces one static binary with
  no new runtime dependency; `cargo test --workspace` green.

input.prompt:
We've approved a new feature for derrick and need it recorded in DESIGN.md as decision **D54**, plus the supporting section edits. You own DESIGN.md; please make the edits directly.

## The feature (approved)

A **native Rust code-graph index** for derrick — a pre-built SQLite + FTS5 index of repository symbols, references, and call relationships that AI agents query directly instead of fanning out across grep/glob/Read. This is the missing "indexing/search/RAG layer" (derrick has none today). It is squarely a **Tokens pillar** feature: it replaces expensive file-reads with cheap structured queries, feeding through the existing scrub/caveman/`derrick gain` machinery.

Inspiration: CodeGraph (https://github.com/colbymchenry/codegraph), a Node/TS tool that does this and benchmarks ~35% cheaper / ~70% fewer tool calls. We are deliberately NOT wrapping it.

## The decisions to lock in D54 (and any sub-entries you think warrant their own D number)

1. **Native Rust, not a Node wrapper.** Preserves the single-static-binary, no-external-runtime, batteries-included ethos and the D11 substrate/scope discipline. We adopt CodeGraph's *data model* (symbols + `references` edges + FTS5) as reference, not its runtime.
2. **MCP server is the agent-facing surface.** `derrick <name> serve --mcp` exposes query tools; `derrick-adopt` wires the MCP stanza into each host's config (Claude Code `mcpServers`, opencode/codex/copilot where supported; document the gap where not, same posture as D34's Codex-hook deferral). This introduces MCP into derrick for the first time — today it uses host CLI subprocess (D30) + hooks (D29). Note this as a new seam. CLI subcommands (`build|search|context|impact|status`) ship too for ad-hoc/Bash parity.
3. **Its own SQLite DB at `.derrick/index.db`, NOT the substrate DB.** Rationale: the AGENTS.md house rule forbids touching SQLite from outside `derrick-substrate-native`; the index has a different schema, a rebuildable-cache lifecycle (gitignored), and a read-heavy concurrency profile. Gitignored via `.derrick/index.db*`.
4. **Focused v1 language scope: Rust, TS/JS, Python, Go.** Symbol index + full-text search + caller/callee/impact. Defer the long tail (20+ langs, framework-aware routes, iOS/RN cross-language bridging).
5. **Pillar alignment**: Tokens (a `derrick gain` line for file-reads avoided / tokens saved, owned by token-economist so numbers reconcile); Memory (seed the index location as reference memory on init); Parallelism (per-file parse fan-out; index DB shared read-only across worktree runs per D38, behind a reader pool like derrick-substrate-native).

## Naming — your call to lock

New crate working name is `derrick-index` / `derrick index …`. The petroleum metaphor lineage (§13) suggests alternatives: **`survey`** (a seismic survey maps subsurface structure before drilling — strong fit for "map the code before working it") or **`core`** (a core sample). Pick the final vocabulary, make sure it doesn't collide with the reserved words (site/ticket/batch/hand/foreman/dispatch/activity) or an existing subcommand, and use it consistently in the edits. Tell me what you chose and why.

# `derrick-survey` — architectural seam sign-off

**Name is settled, not TBD.** DESIGN.md §3.1 (line 133), §9.B.8 (lines 1750-1765), and decisions **D54/D55** (lines 2063-2064) all lock the crate as **`derrick-survey`** with the vocabulary rationale at line 2098 (`survey` = seismic survey, chosen over `core`). The implementer must use `crates/derrick-survey`, command surface `derrick survey build|search|context|impact|status` and `derrick survey serve --mcp`, config under `tools.survey` (DB at `.derrick/index.db`, `reader_pool` default 4). Do not introduce `derrick-index`/`derrick-core`.

## 1. Public API — concrete struct, no trait (v1)

Expose a single concrete `Survey` struct, not a `CodeIndex` trait. Justification against derrick's conventions: `Substrate` is a trait because D11/§8.1 explicitly anticipate *multiple swappable backends* (native, future hosted) behind one contract, and that swap is a product decision. `Stack` is a trait for the same reason (native/graphite/git-spice). D54(a) commits the opposite for survey: **"native Rust, not a Node wrapper"** — there is exactly one intended implementation and no plan for a second backend. A trait here would be speculative generality violating the "narrow traits, expose the minimum" working agreement. Mirror `NativeSubstrate`'s shape: a `Clone` struct holding `Arc<ReaderPool>` + writer mutex, opened via `Survey::open(SurveyConfig) -> Result<Self, SurveyError>`.

Query surface (all `async`, all returning typed structs that are `serde::Serialize` so the CLI and MCP layers share one serialization path):

```
async fn build(&self, opts: BuildOptions) -> Result<BuildReport, SurveyError>   // full or incremental
async fn search(&self, q: &str, limit: usize) -> Result<Vec<SymbolHit>, SurveyError>   // FTS5
async fn context(&self, q: &str) -> Result<SymbolContext, SurveyError>          // symbol + neighbours
async fn impact(&self, symbol: &SymbolRef) -> Result<ImpactSet, SurveyError>    // transitive callers
async fn status(&self) -> Result<IndexStatus, SurveyError>                      // file count, staleness, schema ver
```

`BuildOptions` carries an incremental flag; `build` diffs `content_hash`/`mtime` against the `files` table and only re-parses changed files. Core types: `SymbolHit`, `SymbolRef{file, name, kind}`, `SymbolContext`, `ImpactSet`, `IndexStatus`. Error type is a `thiserror` `SurveyError` *inside* the crate (per the architect error pattern); CLI/MCP boundaries convert to `anyhow`. **The CLI handler and the MCP server both call the same `Survey` methods** — the MCP layer is a thin adapter that maps the 4 query methods to MCP tools and serializes results; it owns no query logic.

## 2. MCP transport — hand-rolled stdio JSON-RPC, NOT `rmcp`

**Verified disqualifier:** `rmcp` (official SDK, latest 1.7.0, May 2026) requires **Rust edition 2024**, which is only available on **Rust ≥ 1.85**. The workspace floor is `rust-version = "1.75"` / `edition = "2021"` (root `Cargo.toml` lines 26-27). `rmcp` cannot compile on this toolchain without a workspace-wide MSRV bump from 1.75 → 1.85 — a ten-version jump that is out of scope for one crate and would need its own decision. It also pulls `schemars`, `reqwest`-with-TLS, and a macro crate for a surface of only ~4 tools.

**Recommendation:** hand-roll a minimal stdio JSON-RPC 2.0 server over `tokio::io::{stdin,stdout}` with line-delimited framing, implementing only `initialize`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`. This adds **zero new dependencies** (`serde_json` + `tokio` are already workspace deps) for ~4 tools. This is also consistent with D54's framing of MCP as "the first MCP seam" — keep it small and owned. Implementer must watch the MCP spec's `initialize` handshake and content-block response envelope; pin the protocol version string.

## 3. FTS5 — available, no extra flag

**Verified:** `rusqlite`'s `bundled` feature (already at workspace `rusqlite = { version="0.39", features=["bundled"] }`, line 44) compiles `libsqlite3-sys` with `-DSQLITE_ENABLE_FTS5` in its `build.rs`. **FTS5 works out of the box; `bundled-full` is NOT needed, no pragma required.** Create the `symbols_fts` virtual table directly in a migration.

## 4. tree-sitter crate selection — pin the 0.23.x grammar line

**Version-pinning hazard confirmed and it is the headline risk.** tree-sitter core 0.26.9 needs Rust 1.77; everything ≥ 0.25 needs ≥ 1.76 — all above the 1.75 floor.

| Crate | Pin | tree-sitter core req | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tree-sitter` | `=0.24.7` | (MSRV 1.65, edition 2021) | newest core that compiles on 1.75 |
| `tree-sitter-rust` | `0.23` | `^0.24` | static C via `cc` build-dep |
| `tree-sitter-typescript` | `0.23` (latest 0.23.2) | `^0.24` | |
| `tree-sitter-python` | `0.23.x` | `^0.24` | verify exact patch at impl time |
| `tree-sitter-go` | `0.23.x` (NOT 0.25.0) | `^0.24` | latest 0.25.0 pulls newer core — do not use |

All grammar crates static-link a generated C parser via a `cc = "^1.1"` build-dependency — no runtime/codegen dependency, preserving the single-static-binary promise. **The implementer must pin exact versions and add a CI check that the build still works on 1.75**, because grammar crates routinely bump their `tree-sitter` requirement in patch releases. Each new dep needs its one-line PR justification (architect rule).

## 5. Parallel build — `rayon` for parse, single serialized writer

Parsing is CPU-bound (tree-sitter is synchronous C); `tokio` tasks are the wrong tool — they'd block the async runtime's worker threads. Use **`rayon`** (new dep; justification: CPU-bound parse fan-out, the canonical use case; aligns with §9.B.8 "per-file parse fan-out... Parallelism pillar"). Pattern: `rayon` par-iterates the changed-file list producing `(File, Vec<Symbol>, Vec<Ref>)` tuples in parallel, results stream to a **single writer task that batches all inserts into one transaction**. This mirrors the substrate's single-writer discipline and avoids SQLite writer contention entirely. Wrap the whole build in `tokio::task::spawn_blocking` so it doesn't stall the async runtime.

## 6. Schema — refined

```sql
files(id INTEGER PK, path TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL, lang TEXT NOT NULL,
      size INTEGER, mtime INTEGER, content_hash TEXT NOT NULL);
symbols(id INTEGER PK, file_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES files(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
        name TEXT NOT NULL, kind TEXT NOT NULL,
        start_line INTEGER, end_line INTEGER, signature TEXT);
refs(src_symbol_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES symbols(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
     dst_symbol_id INTEGER REFERENCES symbols(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
     kind TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE symbols_fts USING fts5(name, signature, content='symbols', content_rowid='id');
```

Refinements over the reference sketch: (a) `ON DELETE CASCADE` on both FKs so incremental rebuild = `DELETE FROM files WHERE path=?` and the symbols/refs vanish; (b) `symbols_fts` as a **contentless/external-content FTS5 table** (`content='symbols'`) to avoid duplicating text — maintain via triggers or rebuild per file; (c) `dst_symbol_id` **nullable** — unresolved references (call to a symbol not in the index, e.g. std/extern) are common and must not be dropped; store the unresolved name in `refs` (add a `dst_name TEXT` column for that case); (d) indexes: `idx_symbols_name(name)`, `idx_symbols_file(file_id)`, `idx_refs_dst(dst_symbol_id)` (impact queries walk this reverse edge), `idx_refs_src(src_symbol_id)`. Use the substrate's migration pattern: `user_version` pragma + `include_str!("../migrations/0001_initial.sql")` (substrate ref: lines 19-22, 1974-1998).

## Risks / things the implementer must watch

1. **MSRV is the dominant constraint.** rmcp (edition 2024) and tree-sitter ≥ 0.25 (rust ≥ 1.76) are both off-limits on the 1.75 floor. Either pin to the versions above, or raise this to design-keeper as a separate decision to bump the workspace MSRV. **Do not silently bump `rust-version`.**
2. **Grammar/core version drift** — exact-pin all five tree-sitter crates and add a 1.75 CI gate; a grammar patch release can break the build.
3. **Own DB, hard boundary (D54c + AGENTS.md house rule).** `derrick-survey` MUST open its own `.derrick/index.db` with its own connection management; it must NOT touch the substrate DB or add tables to it. Replicate the substrate's reader-pool + writer-mutex pattern (lines 531-560, 1942-1972) rather than sharing connections.
4. **Enable WAL.** The substrate does *not* set `journal_mode=WAL` (it uses `busy_timeout=5000` + `synchronous=NORMAL`, lines 1961-1972). The survey DB is read-heavy with many concurrent worktree readers (D38) and an infrequent writer — it **should** add `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL` so readers never block on the rebuild writer. This is a deliberate divergence from the substrate; call it out in the PR.
5. **`spawn_blocking` discipline** — all rusqlite and all tree-sitter parsing is synchronous/blocking; every DB and parse call must be inside `spawn_blocking` (or rayon under one `spawn_blocking`) or it will stall the tokio runtime. Same rule the substrate follows (line 537, 552).
6. **New deps needing PR justification:** `rayon` (CPU parse fan-out), `tree-sitter` + 4 grammar crates, and a hashing crate for `content_hash` (prefer a small one, e.g. `blake3` or `seahash`; check if anything in the lock already provides one before adding).

Sources:
- [rmcp on crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/rmcp)
- [modelcontextprotocol/rust-sdk](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/rust-sdk)
- [tree-sitter on crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/tree-sitter)
- [rusqlite libsqlite3-sys build.rs (FTS5 flags)](https://github.com/rusqlite/rusqlite/blob/master/libsqlite3-sys/build.rs)

One open item worth a quick design-keeper note: **the MSRV decision**. If the team would rather use `rmcp` and current tree-sitter, that requires a workspace MSRV bump to ≥ 1.85 — that is a D-entry, not something the implementation pass should decide unilaterally. # `derrick-survey` — architectural seam sign-off

**Name is settled, not TBD.** DESIGN.md §3.1 (line 133), §9.B.8 (lines 1750-1765), and decisions **D54/D55** (lines 2063-2064) all lock the crate as **`derrick-survey`** with the vocabulary rationale at line 2098 (`survey` = seismic survey, chosen over `core`). The implementer must use `crates/derrick-survey`, command surface `derrick survey build|search|context|impact|status` and `derrick survey serve --mcp`, config under `tools.survey` (DB at `.derrick/index.db`, `reader_pool` default 4). Do not introduce `derrick-index`/`derrick-core`.

## 1. Public API — concrete struct, no trait (v1)

Expose a single concrete `Survey` struct, not a `CodeIndex` trait. Justification against derrick's conventions: `Substrate` is a trait because D11/§8.1 explicitly anticipate *multiple swappable backends* (native, future hosted) behind one contract, and that swap is a product decision. `Stack` is a trait for the same reason (native/graphite/git-spice). D54(a) commits the opposite for survey: **"native Rust, not a Node wrapper"** — there is exactly one intended implementation and no plan for a second backend. A trait here would be speculative generality violating the "narrow traits, expose the minimum" working agreement. Mirror `NativeSubstrate`'s shape: a `Clone` struct holding `Arc<ReaderPool>` + writer mutex, opened via `Survey::open(SurveyConfig) -> Result<Self, SurveyError>`.

Query surface (all `async`, all returning typed structs that are `serde::Serialize` so the CLI and MCP layers share one serialization path):

```
async fn build(&self, opts: BuildOptions) -> Result<BuildReport, SurveyError>   // full or incremental
async fn search(&self, q: &str, limit: usize) -> Result<Vec<SymbolHit>, SurveyError>   // FTS5
async fn context(&self, q: &str) -> Result<SymbolContext, SurveyError>          // symbol + neighbours
async fn impact(&self, symbol: &SymbolRef) -> Result<ImpactSet, SurveyError>    // transitive callers
async fn status(&self) -> Result<IndexStatus, SurveyError>                      // file count, staleness, schema ver
```

`BuildOptions` carries an incremental flag; `build` diffs `content_hash`/`mtime` against the `files` table and only re-parses changed files. Core types: `SymbolHit`, `SymbolRef{file, name, kind}`, `SymbolContext`, `ImpactSet`, `IndexStatus`. Error type is a `thiserror` `SurveyError` *inside* the crate (per the architect error pattern); CLI/MCP boundaries convert to `anyhow`. **The CLI handler and the MCP server both call the same `Survey` methods** — the MCP layer is a thin adapter that maps the 4 query methods to MCP tools and serializes results; it owns no query logic.

## 2. MCP transport — hand-rolled stdio JSON-RPC, NOT `rmcp`

**Verified disqualifier:** `rmcp` (official SDK, latest 1.7.0, May 2026) requires **Rust edition 2024**, which is only available on **Rust ≥ 1.85**. The workspace floor is `rust-version = "1.75"` / `edition = "2021"` (root `Cargo.toml` lines 26-27). `rmcp` cannot compile on this toolchain without a workspace-wide MSRV bump from 1.75 → 1.85 — a ten-version jump that is out of scope for one crate and would need its own decision. It also pulls `schemars`, `reqwest`-with-TLS, and a macro crate for a surface of only ~4 tools.

**Recommendation:** hand-roll a minimal stdio JSON-RPC 2.0 server over `tokio::io::{stdin,stdout}` with line-delimited framing, implementing only `initialize`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`. This adds **zero new dependencies** (`serde_json` + `tokio` are already workspace deps) for ~4 tools. This is also consistent with D54's framing of MCP as "the first MCP seam" — keep it small and owned. Implementer must watch the MCP spec's `initialize` handshake and content-block response envelope; pin the protocol version string.

## 3. FTS5 — available, no extra flag

**Verified:** `rusqlite`'s `bundled` feature (already at workspace `rusqlite = { version="0.39", features=["bundled"] }`, line 44) compiles `libsqlite3-sys` with `-DSQLITE_ENABLE_FTS5` in its `build.rs`. **FTS5 works out of the box; `bundled-full` is NOT needed, no pragma required.** Create the `symbols_fts` virtual table directly in a migration.

## 4. tree-sitter crate selection — pin the 0.23.x grammar line

**Version-pinning hazard confirmed and it is the headline risk.** tree-sitter core 0.26.9 needs Rust 1.77; everything ≥ 0.25 needs ≥ 1.76 — all above the 1.75 floor.

| Crate | Pin | tree-sitter core req | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tree-sitter` | `=0.24.7` | (MSRV 1.65, edition 2021) | newest core that compiles on 1.75 |
| `tree-sitter-rust` | `0.23` | `^0.24` | static C via `cc` build-dep |
| `tree-sitter-typescript` | `0.23` (latest 0.23.2) | `^0.24` | |
| `tree-sitter-python` | `0.23.x` | `^0.24` | verify exact patch at impl time |
| `tree-sitter-go` | `0.23.x` (NOT 0.25.0) | `^0.24` | latest 0.25.0 pulls newer core — do not use |

All grammar crates static-link a generated C parser via a `cc = "^1.1"` build-dependency — no runtime/codegen dependency, preserving the single-static-binary promise. **The implementer must pin exact versions and add a CI check that the build still works on 1.75**, because grammar crates routinely bump their `tree-sitter` requirement in patch releases. Each new dep needs its one-line PR justification (architect rule).

## 5. Parallel build — `rayon` for parse, single serialized writer

Parsing is CPU-bound (tree-sitter is synchronous C); `tokio` tasks are the wrong tool — they'd block the async runtime's worker threads. Use **`rayon`** (new dep; justification: CPU-bound parse fan-out, the canonical use case; aligns with §9.B.8 "per-file parse fan-out... Parallelism pillar"). Pattern: `rayon` par-iterates the changed-file list producing `(File, Vec<Symbol>, Vec<Ref>)` tuples in parallel, results stream to a **single writer task that batches all inserts into one transaction**. This mirrors the substrate's single-writer discipline and avoids SQLite writer contention entirely. Wrap the whole build in `tokio::task::spawn_blocking` so it doesn't stall the async runtime.

## 6. Schema — refined

```sql
files(id INTEGER PK, path TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL, lang TEXT NOT NULL,
      size INTEGER, mtime INTEGER, content_hash TEXT NOT NULL);
symbols(id INTEGER PK, file_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES files(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
        name TEXT NOT NULL, kind TEXT NOT NULL,
        start_line INTEGER, end_line INTEGER, signature TEXT);
refs(src_symbol_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES symbols(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
     dst_symbol_id INTEGER REFERENCES symbols(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
     kind TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE symbols_fts USING fts5(name, signature, content='symbols', content_rowid='id');
```

Refinements over the reference sketch: (a) `ON DELETE CASCADE` on both FKs so incremental rebuild = `DELETE FROM files WHERE path=?` and the symbols/refs vanish; (b) `symbols_fts` as a **contentless/external-content FTS5 table** (`content='symbols'`) to avoid duplicating text — maintain via triggers or rebuild per file; (c) `dst_symbol_id` **nullable** — unresolved references (call to a symbol not in the index, e.g. std/extern) are common and must not be dropped; store the unresolved name in `refs` (add a `dst_name TEXT` column for that case); (d) indexes: `idx_symbols_name(name)`, `idx_symbols_file(file_id)`, `idx_refs_dst(dst_symbol_id)` (impact queries walk this reverse edge), `idx_refs_src(src_symbol_id)`. Use the substrate's migration pattern: `user_version` pragma + `include_str!("../migrations/0001_initial.sql")` (substrate ref: lines 19-22, 1974-1998).

## Risks / things the implementer must watch

1. **MSRV is the dominant constraint.** rmcp (edition 2024) and tree-sitter ≥ 0.25 (rust ≥ 1.76) are both off-limits on the 1.75 floor. Either pin to the versions above, or raise this to design-keeper as a separate decision to bump the workspace MSRV. **Do not silently bump `rust-version`.**
2. **Grammar/core version drift** — exact-pin all five tree-sitter crates and add a 1.75 CI gate; a grammar patch release can break the build.
3. **Own DB, hard boundary (D54c + AGENTS.md house rule).** `derrick-survey` MUST open its own `.derrick/index.db` with its own connection management; it must NOT touch the substrate DB or add tables to it. Replicate the substrate's reader-pool + writer-mutex pattern (lines 531-560, 1942-1972) rather than sharing connections.
4. **Enable WAL.** The substrate does *not* set `journal_mode=WAL` (it uses `busy_timeout=5000` + `synchronous=NORMAL`, lines 1961-1972). The survey DB is read-heavy with many concurrent worktree readers (D38) and an infrequent writer — it **should** add `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL` so readers never block on the rebuild writer. This is a deliberate divergence from the substrate; call it out in the PR.
5. **`spawn_blocking` discipline** — all rusqlite and all tree-sitter parsing is synchronous/blocking; every DB and parse call must be inside `spawn_blocking` (or rayon under one `spawn_blocking`) or it will stall the tokio runtime. Same rule the substrate follows (line 537, 552).
6. **New deps needing PR justification:** `rayon` (CPU parse fan-out), `tree-sitter` + 4 grammar crates, and a hashing crate for `content_hash` (prefer a small one, e.g. `blake3` or `seahash`; check if anything in the lock already provides one before adding).

Files referenced: `/Users/lgulliver/repos/derrick/Cargo.toml` (lines 26-27 MSRV, 44 rusqlite); `/Users/lgulliver/repos/derrick/crates/derrick-substrate-native/src/lib.rs` (lines 19-22 migrations, 34-41 struct, 531-560 read/write helpers, 1942-1972 connection PRAGMAs, 1974-1998 migrate); `/Users/lgulliver/repos/derrick/crates/derrick-substrate/src/lib.rs` (lines 20-21 trait pattern); `/Users/lgulliver/repos/derrick/DESIGN.md` (line 133 §3.1, lines 1750-1765 §9.B.8, lines 2063-2064 D54/D55, line 2098 naming).

Sources:
- [rmcp on crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/rmcp)
- [modelcontextprotocol/rust-sdk](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/rust-sdk)
- [tree-sitter on crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/tree-sitter)
- [rusqlite libsqlite3-sys build.rs (FTS5 flags)](https://github.com/rusqlite/rusqlite/blob/master/libsqlite3-sys/build.rs)

One open item worth a quick design-keeper note: **the MSRV decision**. If the team would rather use `rmcp` and current tree-sitter, that requires a workspace MSRV bump to ≥ 1.85 — that is a D-entry, not something the implementation pass should decide unilaterally. My recommendation is to hold the 1.75 floor and ship with the pinned versions + hand-rolled MCP as above.
